record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Operational forestry planning currently treats short-horizon harvesting and transportation sequentially, even though daily and weekly harvest choices determine the data that truck schedulers receive. The open question is how to build and solve a single detailed model that jointly schedules short-term harvesting activities and transportation decisions over daily or weekly periods.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 How can we model and solve the scheduling of jointly detailed daily or weekly harvesting and transportation decisions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an operational forest-management setting over a short planning horizon discretized into days (or weeks) t = 1, ..., T. The following data are given:

- A set H of harvest units (stands), each with available standing volume by product/assortment a ∈ A, and access constraints (e.g., road availability, seasonal restrictions).
- A set M of harvesting machines (felling, processing, forwarding) with daily productivities, mobilization/relocation costs, and minimum dwell times on a stand.
- A set R of roadside storage points and a road network linking stands to a set D of demand points (mills, terminals).
- A fleet K of trucks, each with capacity, daily availability windows, driver shift rules, loading/unloading times, and travel times along the network.
- Daily demands d_{j,a,t} at each mill j ∈ D for each assortment a, with possible inventory bounds at roadside and at mills.

Decision variables jointly model, for every day t:
(i) which stands are harvested, by which machines, and how much volume of each assortment is produced and placed at roadside;
(ii) machine relocations between stands;
(iii) truck dispatch decisions: routes, loads, sequence of pickups and deliveries, and resulting inventories at roadside and at mills.

Formulate a single mixed-integer optimization model that simultaneously decides the short-term harvesting schedule and the detailed transportation schedule over the horizon, with an objective combining harvesting cost, machine relocation cost, transportation cost, inventory cost, and penalties for unmet demand, subject to flow conservation of timber from stumps to mills, machine and truck capacity/time constraints, and roadside inventory balance.

Problem: Construct such an integrated model in sufficient detail to be operationally meaningful, and design an exact or heuristic solution method that can solve instances of realistic industrial size (hundreds of stands, tens of machines and trucks, several mills, horizons of one to several weeks) within computation times acceptable for daily operational planning.
artifact.status_search_result: Several integrated MILP models for jointly scheduling short-term harvesting and transportation of forest products at daily/weekly granularity have been proposed since the question was posed (e.g., Bordón et al., Forests 2019; metaheuristic approaches in Operational Research 2021; simulation-based multi-objective studies in 2025; and a "Forestry 4.0" integrated framework in 2024). These works provide formulations and solution heuristics, but no single fully scalable exact method is universally accepted for industrial instances, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved with active ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: A Mathematical Model for the Integrated Optimization of Harvest and Transport Scheduling of Forest Products
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a novel optimization model for daily and weekly planning of harvesting operations, minimizing machinery, movement and transport costs subject to demand constraints; notes no prior work addressed integrated harvest-transport scheduling at daily/weekly horizon.
status_evidence.claim: An integrated daily/weekly MILP formulation for joint harvest and transport scheduling has been published.

status_evidence.title: Solving the integrated forest harvest scheduling model using metaheuristic algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Develops metaheuristic algorithms for the integrated forest harvest scheduling model.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic solution approaches to integrated harvest-transport scheduling have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Simulation-based multi-objective optimization to support delivery performance decisions in harvest scheduling and transport
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) multi-objective simulation-optimization combining harvest scheduling and transport decisions.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues into integrated harvest-transport scheduling, indicating the problem remains an active topic.

status_evidence.title: Smart forestry – a forestry 4.0 approach to intelligent and fully integrated timber harvesting
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses fully integrated timber harvesting frameworks.
status_evidence.claim: Integration efforts continue under Forestry 4.0 paradigms.
